items.summary: The selectedModel prop chain: chat-header renders <ModelSelector>, chat-page-content and the use-chat-conversation / use-streaming-chat hooks carry the id into the request body. No alias literals; pure pass-through.
items.removalGate: Keep. Recorded so the epic's edit list is complete: these four files must be visited if the model id's TYPE changes, even though none of them hard-codes a value.

items.name: App model API route constants
items.summary: Two route constants the app uses for model data: '/analytics/models' and '/v1/models'. The former feeds the credits panel's per-model breakdown.
items.removalGate: Keep. Both endpoints must keep returning Alia aliases only; /analytics/models is rendered directly to end users in the credits panel, so it is a live abstraction-leak surface if the API ever resolves a raw provider model id there.

items.name: @alia.onl/sdk model defaults
items.summary: The published SDK's model surface: a `model` prop defaulting to 'alia-v1' (documented on AliaChatScreen and AliaChatSheet) plus two voice paths pinned to 'alia-v1-voice'. No model PICKER ships in the SDK — the consumer passes an id.
items.removalGate: Keep, and treat these three literals as the highest-inertia alias references in the repo: they are compiled into external consumers' apps (the package ships as RAW SOURCE), so retiring alia-v1 or alia-v1-voice breaks installed SDK versions that no Alia deploy can fix. Any alias retirement plan must keep both ids resolvable indefinitely or ship a major SDK version first. Verified there is no model picker component in the SDK: all 49 files under packages/alia-chat/src were enumerated.

items.name: Codea webview model picker
items.summary: In-editor chat model dropdown. Fetches the catalog from the API but ships a one-entry defaultModels fallback and a hard-coded initial state, both 'alia-v1-codea'.
items.removalGate: Keep. Same shipped-binary inertia as the SDK: a VS Code extension in the marketplace keeps sending 'alia-v1-codea' until each user updates.

items.name: Codea VS Code settings + providers
items.summary: The codea.model contributed setting defaults to 'alia-v1-codea'; three extension entry points read it with the same literal as their fallback (chat participant, chat provider, inline completions).
items.removalGate: Keep. The setting is correctly documented as 'available models are fetched from the API', and it is a free-form string rather than an enum, so the catalog can grow without an extension release — only the DEFAULT is frozen. Also update packages/alia-codea/README.md:15,63, which list alias ids in prose.

items.name: Codea CLI model defaults
items.summary: Three commander --model options defaulting to 'alia-v1-codea', plus the config default and the sessions fallback. The TUI strips the 'alia-v1-' prefix for display.
items.removalGate: Keep. One defect to fix while here: the --model help text advertises short names ('codea, codea-pro, codea-thinking') while the default is a full alias id — the two vocabularies disagree, and 'codea-pro'/'codea-thinking' correspond to no defined alias. Also update packages/alia-codea-cli/README.md:125.

items.name: Cowork model picker and defaults
items.summary: Electron renderer chat picker with a one-entry 'alia-v1-cowork' fallback and initial state; the main process pins the same alias in auth.ts and chat.ts, and the tool layer pins 'alia-v1-browser' for browser automation.
items.removalGate: Keep. Note tools.ts:454 pins alia-v1-browser with the inline comment 'Browser automation specialist model' — a capability-to-alias binding hard-coded in a desktop binary, which is the pattern most likely to break silently when relay owns capability routing.

items.name: Canvas model list and workflow node defaults
items.summary: fetchModels() reads GET /v1/models with a one-entry 'alia-lite' fallback; the workflow editor and node edit panel seed every AI node with 'alia-lite'. Also exports a deprecated static MODELS alias of the fallback.
items.removalGate: Keep. Included because canvas was not named in the brief but carries six alias sites and its own /v1/models client — an alias-retirement sweep that skips it leaves saved workflow nodes pinned to a dead id. The `MODELS` export at models.ts:42 is a back-compat alias with a comment saying it will be replaced; it should be deleted rather than carried forward.

items.name: shared-types AliaTier union
items.summary: The declared canonical superset of Alia tiers (14 members) plus the AliaModel / ModelCapabilities DTOs. Explicitly documented as provider-agnostic by construction.
items.removalGate: Keep and make it authoritative. It calls itself 'the canonical superset', yet the gateway admin maintains a SECOND, DIFFERENT 12-member list (missing v1-tts and v1-image) with no type relationship between them. Retiring the gateway admin removes that fork for free — which is an argument for doing workstream 9 early rather than late.
